title: Arcade Fire · The Suburbs
description: Handmade houses and miniature cars line an empty street at blue hour. Porch lamps warm the edges of the paper sky.

performance.lyrics: Ah with silver bazaar long to drive and told me you will never survive. Grab your mother's keys, we're leaving. Ah You always seem so sure that one day we fight in the suburban world. Your part of town against mine, I saw you standing on the opposite shore. But by the the first bombs fell, we were already bored. We were already, already bored. Sometimes I can't it. I'm moving past a feeling. Sometimes I can't believe it, I'm movin' past the feelin' again kids wanna be so hard But in my dreams where's the screamin' and runnin' Ah and all of the walls that they built in the 70s finally fall, all of the houses they built in the 70s finally fall it meant nothing at all it meant nothing at all it meant nothing. Sometimes I can't it, I'm moving past the feeling. Sometimes I can't believe it, I'm moving past the feeling into the night. Ah So can you understand I want a daughter while I'm still young? won't hold her hand, show her some beauty before all this damage is done. But if it's too much to ask, if it's too much to ask They sent me a son The overpass, the parking lot was new, it's already passed. So move your feet from hot pavement into the grass, because it's already passed. It's already, already past. Sometimes I can't it I'm moving past the feeling Sometimes I can't it I'm moving past the feeling again I will move very fast, the finger in I will move very fast, figure in Ah We're still screaming, Ah we're we're is screaming. Ah Ah
